native_result.query: In the PCA on the forms of capital analyzed in hundred-year time slices, during the Younger Bronze Age (1100-500 BCE), how does the principal component value of PC1 in the beginning of the period at 1100 BCE differ from the subsequent time horizons between 1000 to 500 BCE?
native_result.HypoA: The beginning of the Younger Bronze Age (1100 BCE) is associated with negative values on the first principal component (PC1), while the majority of time horizons (1000-500 BCE) are characterized by positive values on PC1. This Principal component analysis (PCA) is on the forms of capital. The values of the individual elements of the forms of capital form the attributes.
native_result.HypoB: The PC1 value at the beginning of the Younger Bronze Age (1100 BCE, score = -4.43) is approximately 3 standard deviations more negative than all subsequent time horizons between 1000 and 500 BCE (scores ranging from -2.13 to -0.78). This extreme negative deviation at 1100 BCE reflects a brief, intense concentration of prestige and wealth capital — particularly copper/gold (Z=2.85), depot finds (Z=3.38), daggers (Z=1.10), house size (Z=1.65), and monument count (Z=1.35) — that rapidly dissipates within one 100-year interval. By 1000 BCE the PC1 score has already shifted by ~2.3 units, and it continues rising gradually toward -0.78 by 500 BCE, indicating a stable post-transition equilibrium in capital composition. The pattern suggests a terminal Bronze Age capital accumulation event at ~1100 BCE that was not sustained into the subsequent YBA.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1. Parsed capital.csv (39 rows × 12 Z variables, comma decimal separator). 2. Verified data already z-scored (mean≈0, std≈1). 3. Dropped 'group' and 'color' columns. 4. Computed 12×12 correlation matrix across all 39 time bins. 5. Performed eigendecomposition to obtain PC1 loadings and scores. 6. Extracted PC1 scores for the 7 YBA bins (1100-500 BCE). 7. Computed differences PC1(1100) - PC1(x) for x = 1000,900,800,700,600,500. 8. Interpreted PC1 loadings in terms of capital types.
